notes.title: Devlog #4: Combat & UI Overhaul
notes.content:
Hello, adventurers! We hope you all had a fantastic holiday season. The team is back, recharged, and excited to dive into 2025 with some big updates. Your feedback from the playtest has been invaluable, and we’ve been hard at work improving the combat system, movement mechanics, and inventory UI to make Godforged: Origins of Ozgalor even better.
This Devlog focuses on key refinements that directly address player requests—so let’s jump in!

⚔️ Target Locking – Smarter, More Intuitive Combat
One of the most requested features from the playtest was better control over targeting during fights. To improve combat flow and precision, we’ve introduced a target-locking system:

- The game now automatically locks onto the closest enemy when you engage in combat, ensuring your attacks and abilities land where you intend.
If multiple enemies are nearby, the system dynamically switches targets based on proximity and player movement.
- Players can also manually switch targets or unlock the focus using the middle mouse button on PC or R3 on a controller, allowing for greater control in fast-paced encounters.
This makes melee and ranged combat smoother, preventing unnecessary misfires or awkward repositioning.
- By automating target selection, combat remains fast-paced and immersive, while still allowing for precise control. We’ll continue refining this system based on feedback, ensuring it strikes the right balance between automation and player agency.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45091242/ab827d37e2bd5a6ad104c3b855fb0f980870be4f.png

🏹 8-Point Movement – More Freedom, More Control
Another major request from players was for greater movement flexibility, especially in combat encounters. We’ve now upgraded the movement system from 4-directional to 8-directional movement, giving characters the ability to move diagonally alongside standard cardinal directions.

- This results in more fluid and responsive character movement, improving both exploration and combat maneuvering.
- Strafing, dodging, and repositioning in fights will feel more natural and intuitive.
- The game world will feel less rigid and more dynamic, making traversal smoother overall.
With this change, movement in Godforged now better aligns with modern ARPG controls, while still maintaining a tactical edge in combat.

🛠️ UI Improvements – A Better Inventory Experience
While refining combat, we also took the time to improve the inventory UI, making it more readable and intuitive.

- Text size and clarity have been improved to ensure better visibility, especially for stats and inventory details.
- The new design is cleaner and more accessible, allowing for easier item management.
- We’ve started implementing more detailed stat tracking, giving players deeper insight into how different gear and abilities affect their playstyle.

The first image below shows the old version of the inventory UI, while the second image showcases the updated version with larger text, better layout, and clearer stats. These adjustments were made based on your feedback, and we’ll continue refining them as development progresses.

Old Inventory UI
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45091242/f04e233886440ccabfb7e3c28bda0130a3533107.png
New Inventory UI
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45091242/f61b26c7b4f65d482677423802283053f4c42588.png

📢 What’s Next?
Your feedback has been instrumental in shaping Godforged, and we’re excited to keep evolving the game with your insights. The improvements in combat control, movement, and UI are just the beginning, and we’ll be sharing more updates soon on upcoming changes.
Let us know what you think of these updates! Do these changes address some of your biggest concerns? Is there anything else you’d like to see improved in movement, targeting, or UI?
We’re grateful for your continued support—this is a game we’re building together with you!

See you in Ozgalor,
The Godforged: Origins of Ozgalor Development Team

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45091242/8755d4ac5603fc280e38bbe087bd6f046b421f81.png

If you've reached this far, we would like to extend a thank you from everyone at Tricoman Studios! Consider joining our Discord and supporting us in our journey to be a part of our story!

notes.title: Devlog #3: Into the Corruption
notes.content:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45091242/a08272a55eea66ea0a9722afe2d540bb247fab2e.png

It’s been a while, Ozgalorians!

We’ve been hard at work preparing a ton of exciting updates for you. As we approach our first public test from December 20th to 22nd, we’re thrilled to share what’s been happening behind the scenes. This test marks the beginning of a series of public trials that will allow you, our players, to experience and help shape Godforged: Origins of Ozgalor. But before we open the gates, let’s dive into the latest developments.

Masselite Corruption: A System of Choices and Consequences

One of the most defining aspects of Godforged: Origins of Ozgalor is the Masselite Corruption System. This core mechanic seamlessly blends narrative and gameplay in a way that feels both fresh and deeply engaging. While this system is still in its conceptual phase and will come with later builds, its full potential will unfold as the game develops. Here’s a preview of what’s in store:

The Essence of Corruption

Masselite is a mysterious and volatile material that powers much of the lands magic and technology. However, its use comes with dire consequences, as it slowly corrupts the environment, creatures, and even items it touches. This corruption serves as the foundation of a multi-layered system that impacts every aspect of the game. Here’s a glimpse of its key components:

Land Corruption: Entire zones in Ozgalor have succumbed to Masselite’s influence. Clearing these corrupted areas not only restores the land but also unlocks new opportunities—such as access to NPCs, vendors, and quests in residential zones. Non-residential zones, on the other hand, transform from barren wastelands back into lush environments teeming with life.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45091242/374de0b4ad4af53f4ae3b4693d18fc5fb3cc87b0.png

Infested Creatures: Corrupted beasts roam the land, ranging from partially afflicted creatures that can still be cleansed to monstrous abominations beyond salvation. Deciding how to deal with these threats—whether through purification or destruction—is a choice that will shape your journey.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45091242/5e88fd8863f54b2d98124a37cc81c805bcdaa0f5.png

Corrupted Items: Rare and powerful artifacts tainted by corruption offer immense potential but at great risk. Players can wield their cursed power or cleanse them to create potent, albeit slightly diminished, relics.

Places of Power: Ancient Dremari altars scattered across Ozgalor have been corrupted, presenting unique challenges and opportunities for those brave enough to cleanse them.

The Corruption Levels

The system operates on two levels—zone corruption and world corruption:

Zone Corruption: Each region’s corruption level fluctuates based on your actions. Reducing it unlocks specific events, restores the area’s vitality, and brings new gameplay opportunities.

World Corruption: This global meter reflects the cumulative impact of player efforts across all zones. As the world corruption level shifts, major events unfold, altering both the narrative and gameplay in significant ways.

Your Role as the Godforged

As a Godforged, you’ll have a critical role in determining how corruption is handled. Infuse it for personal gain, earning Masselite skill points that enhance your powers—but beware, as this increases your own corruption and affects how the world perceives you. Alternatively, destroy the source of corruption to restore balance without personal risk, though this path offers fewer immediate rewards. These decisions will have lasting consequences, making every choice a pivotal moment in your journey.

While this is just a glimpse of the system’s potential, we’re excited to showcase how Masselite Corruption shapes the world of Godforged: Origins of Ozgalor. More details will unfold as the game evolves. So stay tuned for future updates!

World and Lore: Crafting the Ebonvale Uplands

While the Masselite Corruption system has been a major focus, our creative team has been tirelessly bringing the world of Ozgalor to life. In this update, we’re proud to reveal some of the work that’s gone into the Ebonvale Uplands and its iconic centerpiece, Castle Ebongard.

The Ebonvale Uplands

This rugged, mountainous region of Ozgalor is a land of stark contrasts—majestic peaks shrouded in mist, lush valleys dotted with ancient ruins, and treacherous paths haunted by corruption. Our environmental artists and concept designers have been hard at work crafting this breathtaking zone, and we’re thrilled to give you a sneak peek into what lies ahead.

Castle Ebongard: Standing as a bastion of hope and resilience, Castle Ebongard is both a fortress and a symbol of the duchy’s storied past. Its towering spires and intricate architecture reflect the strength and determination of those who call it home. The design of this castle blends rich historical influences with the fantastical elements of Ozgalor, creating a location that feels both grounded and awe-inspiring.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45091242/e11e4380c5283a5e8e7f7f2c122ed9861f9fa34c.png

Secrets of Ozgalor: Over the next few months, we’ll be showcasing some of the stunning concept art and environmental designs that bring the Ebonvale Uplands to life. From misty forests to ancient ruins, every detail has been crafted to immerse players in the world of Godforged.

We’re excited to share more about the Ebonvale Uplands and Castle Ebongard in early 2025, including behind-the-scenes looks at the creative process and additional previews of this captivating new zone.

Community Spotlight: Gamescon Serbia

In November, we had the incredible opportunity to showcase Godforged at Gamescon Serbia, where we connected with fans and shared our progress. Meeting so many of you in person was both humbling and inspiring. Your enthusiasm, questions, and feedback remind us why we’re creating this game in the first place.

Highlights from the event included:

Live Demos: Attendees had the chance to try the build early, providing us with valuable insights into gameplay balance and pacing.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45091242/1319baa52ac1400215bc258c75f82061830a8bcb.jpg

Community Engagement: Hearing your stories and seeing your excitement reaffirmed our commitment to delivering a game that exceeds expectations.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45091242/97a06c8e604e4a08711c9e5b3888a55ca6c974ad.png

We’re incredibly grateful for the support of our community and can’t wait to see how your feedback shapes the future of Godforged.

Looking Ahead

The public test on December 20th - 22nd is just the beginning. As we move forward, we’ll continue to refine and expand the world of Godforged, drawing on your feedback to make the game the best it can be. Here’s what to expect in the coming months:

Early 2025: A deep dive into the Ebonvale Uplands, bundled with new stories, characters, and gameplay features.
Future Updates: More on the Masselite Corruption System, castle-building mechanics, and the rich lore of Ozgalor.

Thank you for being part of this journey. Your support means the world to us, and we’re excited to have you by our side as we continue this adventure together.

Until next time, stay curious, stay courageous, and most importantly—stay Godforged

And a big thanks to you!
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45091242/8755d4ac5603fc280e38bbe087bd6f046b421f81.png

notes.title: Godforged Devlog #1 - An Intro and a Thank You
notes.content:
A Hearty Hello for Devlog #1
Hello adventurers,
FIrst we’d like to extend a heartfelt thank you to everyone who participated in our early survey for Godforged: Origins of Ozgalor all the way back in October 2023. Your insights have been instrumental in guiding the development of the game, from worldbuilding and narrative to gameplay mechanics and design choices. Today, we want to share a glimpse into the intricate web of lore, history, and storylines that form the foundation of Ozgalor, alongside other exciting aspects that make the game a unique experience.

Worldbuilding: Laying the Groundwork for Epic Tales
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45091242/71d02ebb0b72de93e24ba1813e9a979a16ed35af.pngBuilding the Archipelago of Ozgalor has been a labor of love, requiring a careful balance of creativity and consistency. Our focus has been on crafting a living, breathing world that feels both ancient and ever-evolving. From the soaring peaks of Rhunpeak to the mysterious depths of Stonecliff Valley, each location is meticulously designed to tell its own story. Inspired by classic fantasy settings and unique twists, every stone, tree, and stream in Ozgalor serves a purpose in the grand narrative. While Ozgalor is central to Godforged: Origins of Ozgalor, it is just one part of the vast world of Nelethar—a world full of regions, mysteries, and narratives yet to be explored. 

Factions, Races, and Cultures: Weaving a Complex Tapestry
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45091242/77286095183e556258f8ce724fe2abd4b7f62a95.pngOzgalor is a land of diversity, with numerous factions and races vying for power, influence, and survival. The disciplined warriors of Eldorath, the mystical Dremari tribes, and the rebellious forces of Ebonhand are just a few of the key players in this world. As you navigate the treacherous politics and alliances, you’ll find that every decision matters. Who will you ally with? Who will you betray? The choices you make will echo throughout the land, influencing the fate of Ozgalor.

The Influence of Masselite: A Double-Edged Sword
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45091242/404b42de99712a8517dc3ed15246567ebbb01f28.pngOne of the central elements of our world is Masselite, a mysterious ore that has the power to both corrupt and empower. Discovered deep within the mines of Stonecliff Valley, Masselite has become a source of both wonder and fear. Its influence can be felt across the land, driving men to madness and awakening ancient forces long thought dormant. How you interact with this powerful resource will shape your journey and the world around you.

Community Engagement
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45091242/d4d4dde354d03e2f0ca9ec9070562dd4d46c751e.pngFinally we’re thrilled to have you all here on Discord, where we can continue to engage directly with the community. We’ve also created an FAQ channel to help answer common questions. If there’s something you want to know that isn’t covered, feel free to ask in the general chat, and we’ll work on updating the FAQ with your queries. Your feedback has been crucial in shaping the game, and we want to keep that conversation going. Whether it’s discussing lore, sharing theories, or just chatting about your thoughts, we’re here to listen and to share more of what’s happening behind the scenes.

Looking Forward
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45091242/c569d2025cecaf06b9e9968e1ec655dd32adb207.pngWe’ve got a lot more to reveal in the coming months, from deep dives into specific locations and characters to sneak peeks at the combat system and narrative choices. This is just the beginning, and we’re excited to have you along for the ride.

And a big thanks to you!
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45091242/8755d4ac5603fc280e38bbe087bd6f046b421f81.png

notes.title: Meet the Tricoman Team #4 - Luka Filipović (CTO & Lead Developer)
notes.content:
Meet the Tricoman Team #4 - Luka Filipović (CTO & Lead Developer)

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45091242/b5426f0407bfa31972a58a53b9de25cb1ea0fca1.jpg
Game Dev Building Blocks
I have a lot of interests, and most of them vary quite a bit. I enjoy playing video games, whether it's single-player for storytelling and immersion, or multiplayer with friends for the competitiveness. I also enjoy traveling and hanging out with friends without relying on technology.

I am a huge fan of sports, starting with love for football and basketball for many years. It was definitely a career option for me to be a sports journalist. In the last 10 years, I have become a huge fan of motorsports like MotoGP and F1, but the biggest of all is the NFL. I'm a curious person who loves to solve problems and has an interest in History. 

When I first started watching the NFL I didn't understand it, but it's quite easy to learn and I was initially hooked by the flashy plays but stayed for the complexity and strategy. It's not just like chess, it's like an RTS game in real life. The amount of preparation for the opponent, the strategy of your attacks and defenses, the real-time decision making and of course, the gladiator-like physical and athletic players clashing - all of it is really fun for me.

What are you currently working on in the game?
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45091242/9b12d29c2be2eff9c7f9a74885bc855dc2767f56.png
My primary responsibility is to bring the game’s vision to life through code. I implement gameplay mechanics, features, and systems that make the game engaging and fun for players. Additionally, I stay updated with the latest industry trends, tools, and best practices. My ultimate goal is to create a seamless and enjoyable gaming experience.

What is your earlist gaming memory?
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45091242/fb0b56e7d01ed42cd8d3a2151efc8fdc42c8eed6.png
One of my earliest gaming memories was playing the NES, which was a gift from my grandpa, and spending countless hours on Super Mario Bros until I finally beat it. My first experience with PC gaming came when I visited one of my cousins or uncles, where I got to try games like Counter-Strike, Half-Life, Warcraft III, Civilization III, GTA 3, and Need for Speed: Porsche Unleashed. I loved every one of them and couldn't wait to get my own PC to conquer all these games.

When I finally got my own PC, I vividly remember installing five games: Warcraft III: The Frozen Throne, Rise of Nations, Call of Duty, Return to Castle Wolfenstein, and Counter-Strike 1.6. Each game had something unique that hooked me: Warcraft had an immersive world and compelling characters; Rise of Nations offered the thrill of changing history and conquering the world; Call of Duty provided a fun way to experience World War II; Wolfenstein was terrifying yet exhilarating; and Counter-Strike was simply super fun.

A few years later, after attending several football and basketball matches, I was introduced to FIFA and Football Manager. These games consumed countless hours of my life. The fun and competition of playing FIFA with friends and the excitement of managing teams in Football Manager, like bringing Ronaldinho to Crvena Zvezda, provided some of my most memorable gaming experiences.

What motivated you to pursue a career in game dev?
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45091242/2866dd745cc690fe662316e173d2dda067926f2e.jpg
I’ve always enjoyed crafting and creating things when I was little (like with LEGO), but I wasn't skilled in art, music, or hands-on crafts. However, I excelled in math and discovered I had a talent for programming. Programming allowed me to create something from scratch, which was incredibly satisfying. When I combined this with my love for games, I experienced a profound sense of accomplishment and joy, especially from the moment I created my first prototype at university. I also had friends with similar aspirations, and together, we pursued our dreams. That’s how I found my path into game development.

What are some highlights from your career?
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45091242/ec4c1aa91522ad4311985948765168cb3d7bd928.jpg
One of the major highlights of my career was creating an RPG prototype for mobile while we were in the Nordeus Hub for 4 months, all while working full-time. We had some knowledge of Unity, but it wasn't enough. However, despite the strict deadline, we achieved and learned a lot during those 4 months. This experience propelled us to where we are now in our journey and proved that we are capable of working as a team and creating games.

And a big thanks to you!
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45091242/8755d4ac5603fc280e38bbe087bd6f046b421f81.png
If you've reached this far, we would like to extend a thank you from everyone at Tricoman Studios! Consider joining our Discord and supporting us in our journey to be a part of our story!

notes.title: Meet the Tricoman Team #3 - Luka Budimir (The Swiss Army Developer)
notes.content:
Meet the Tricoman Team #3 - Luka Budimir (The Swiss Army Developer)

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45091242/9d3e13c2ebfb0358902906ae5f4a07eceaf268cc.jpg
Game Dev Building Blocks
At the beginning, something that I could connect to what I'm currently doing definitely would include an interest in Lego. Since I was little, I was obsessed with building my own things out of Lego bricks, creating my own playground and then adding some rules and life to that world, playing their "story". While it entertained me and I enjoyed building those worlds, I enjoyed destroying them and rebuilding everything into a new world, I guess that's very connected with my creative flow, I want to try as much as I can before I figure out what FEELS right.

Sometime in 2011, Minecraft was still a new thing, and with my obsession with Lego, I was really into Minecraft as a concept. As I was mining, building, and repeating the cycle endlessly, I realized I really enjoyed building things in Minecraft. Soon after, I started creating worlds with my friends. When we discovered mods, we began organizing events like "Fellowship Goes to Moria" and similar scenarios which really expanded what I thought was possible in games.

Besides that what i really enjoyed, apart from gaming, was photography. I really enjoy capturing interesting moments in life, probably most of all i enjoy shooting nature and landscapes, which again connects to environment art that i enjoy working on.

What are you currently working on in the game?
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45091242/77843bd0c5782d11db6be3f61efd7f81c9487f84.jpg
In this game, I have narrowed down my roles a bit; currently, I am working on Game / Level design, Environment Art, Tech Art, and VFX. Depending on the current segment of development, I switch roles like Mystique from the Marvel Universe.

Essentially I make sure the entire team stays connected, assist where I can, as well as push myself to do what I love most which is Level and Game design. Creating something out of seemingly nothing brings me too much joy not to pursue.

What is your earlist gaming memory?
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45091242/d0184e80ba474fc5cc424614847a3c6561e5e2b8.jpg[Source]
My introduction to gaming was through the PlayStation 1 console. My father got me a second-hand PS1 in the year 2000. The games I loved the most on that console were Colin McRae Rally 2.0, which I played for thousands of hours, racing against my father and his friends on various tracks. Besides that game, I also enjoyed Medal of Honor—I was amazed by the graphics and still think it has one of the best main menus to this day—as well as Spyro the Dragon, Emperor's New Groove, Tomb Raider, and Lego Racers to spice things up.

On the PC side, I initially really enjoyed shooter games like Wolfenstein: Return to Castle, Battlefield Vietnam, and of course, the Medal of Honor and Call of Duty franchises. Among racing games, Need for Speed: Most Wanted (2005) stands out as the best for me; no racing game has captivated me like that one, especially with the amazing soundtrack.

When it comes to RPGs, World of Warcraft blew my mind. I remember the first time I saw the game in 2006 when I was visiting one of my fathers close friends who was really into gaming. He was on a gryphon ride flying above Azeroth, and it was literally love at first sight. As soon as I got home, I installed WoW right away with that 30-day trial, and the rest is history.

What motivated you to pursue a career in game dev?
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45091242/36b519aa1c5142712522f4cea9e983bf92672839.jpg
Feeling limited by the blocks in Minecraft, I discovered a 3D software called Maya 2014 while I was in high school. After unlocking some modeling skills, I wanted to bring my models to life, so my next stop on the journey was Unity 3D. It had a very user-friendly interface and was popular at the time for being beginner-friendly, which it was. Soon after, I created some shooter prototypes by watching YouTube videos. Not much has changed these days; I switched from Maya to Blender and focused more on visuals rather than programming.

What are some highlights from your career?
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45091242/c5a309db63d3ca2caf8b8efdfa7a6254b9a3b423.jpg
The biggest leap in my game dev career was when "me and the bois" started working on our first RPG game that we wanted to publish on mobile. We applied for a Nordeus mentorship and accelerator program called Booster, where we had the task to build a prototype in 4 months. Challenge accepted, we said. The first step was to move in together, and luckily, a close friend lived alone and had a perfect home office that fit four desktop setups. Check.

Next, we needed to come up with a general idea. We wanted something simpler graphically, so we decided on a top-down perspective to avoid worrying about distance drawing and other complexities. We looked at the available mentors through the program and started having meetups right away while simultaneously developing our game. We finished something you could call a prototype. It was a cool project—nothing special—but we gained huge knowledge during the process, which has led me to where I am now. And that project coincidentally, was the inception of what would become Godforged: Origins of Ozgalor!

And a big thanks to you!
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45091242/8755d4ac5603fc280e38bbe087bd6f046b421f81.png
If you've reached this far, we would like to extend a thank you from everyone at Tricoman Studios! Consider joining our Discord and supporting us in our journey to be a part of our story!

notes.title: Meet the Tricoman Team #2 - Marko Ristic (Narrative & Franchise Director)
notes.content:
Meet the Tricoman Team #2 - Marko Ristic (Narrative & Franchise Director)
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45091242/1b669ced1350833ece284d52c6a23cfc733c101f.jpg
From Dreams to Reality
"He’s living in his own world," was something I heard often, especially when I was younger. Ever since I can remember, I had a tendency to create stories in my head—imagining potential outcomes in real life or crafting tales with my own characters and even those of others. One of my favorite pastimes was daydreaming about alternate endings and new plots for existing stories. For instance, I would envision scenarios where Arthas didn’t turn evil in Reign of Chaos or imagine myself as a supreme mage in the Elder Scrolls universe, altering major events.

Growing up, I was always a bit of a dreamer. My childhood was filled with books, games, and endless daydreams that transported me to other worlds. This love for storytelling wasn't just another fun thing to do; it became a part of who I am. My family and friends often noticed my knack for creating elaborate stories, and while some may have thought I was just a kid with a wild imagination, I knew there was something more to it.

Intro to Storytelling
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45091242/f895222eb60f35c7573f787e097a02a0e4178dcf.jpg
In high school, I created Nelethar, a world that has evolved multiple times over the years. It started as a novel, then became a visual novel, transitioned into an audiobook, and eventually morphed into a video game. Each iteration refined the story and deepened my connection to this world.

During high school and college, I had the privilege to experience a plethora of things—from parties to vacations, meeting new people, and getting introduced to the game development industry. As I grew, so did my world. Finally, in college, together with my two friends, we decided to create Tricoman, meaning three game junkies, and give a shot at creating our first RPG set in the world of Nelethar. However, we soon realized the magnitude of making an RPG. Even though we had assistance from multiple accelerators, it took us several years and the introduction of the newest member of Tricoman, Borislav, to give this project another chance. That’s where we are now, giving it another go at creating a first complete experience in the world of Nelethar through the game Godforged: Origins of Ozgalor.

What are you currently working on the game?
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45091242/234b4ef54a19fab2b23a75ac5798b813c94b47cc.jpg
Right now, I'm deep into working on the lore—lots and lots of lore. Don’t get me wrong, I’m having a blast creating a franchise like this, but it’s definitely not something that can be done overnight. Developing various zones, their histories, heroes, villains, and everything else feels more like being a surgeon than a narrative director. Having to carefully assemble everything and ensure it all makes sense took a lot more than what I originally thought, but at the same time, I haven't had this much fun in a long while.

What is your earliest gaming memory?
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45091242/b4a13edf218655a54c88dee1e73e7920675ffe44.jpg
Ah, my earliest gaming memory... I guess I would have to say it was the first time I played a console game, which was Donkey Kong Country on the SNES. It was my introduction to gaming, and together with my brother, we ended up spending days trying to beat the game in co-op. That experience hooked me immediately, especially since those games had a rather high difficulty with long distances between checkpoints, making us invest more time and effort to pass the levels.

Soon after, we switched to the PS1, playing various games from Crash Bandicoot 1, 2, and 3 to Digimon World 3. We were completely enthralled by the experiences those games offered. Although I started my gaming journey on consoles, it wasn't until I tried GTA Liberty City and Gothic 3 that I fell in love with RPG worlds. Those games made me realize the vast potential and immersive experiences that the world of gaming had to offer and made me fall in love with games even more.

What motivated you to pursue a career in game dev?
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45091242/3e8a932d6e06e85b701c200b0ffd63e14847ddf1.jpg
Stubbornness and love. I've always been passionate about video games and dreamed of creating one of my own. I knew making games was really hard, especially living in the Balkans where opportunities in the game industry are quite limited. Despite this, I held onto the dream of crafting my own story, particularly in an RPG. However, the more I tried, the more feedback I received telling me it was impossible to achieve that in Serbia. Many suggested I should stick to mobile games or writing books—anything that could earn me money instead of wasting time on what seemed impossible.

Just as my passion was starting to dim, I was fortunate enough to meet a mentor who rekindled my hope. Soon after, like a domino effect, I began meeting people from around the world who pushed me to greater heights. Eventually, I was offered what was previously my dream job at Blizzard Entertainment. However, at the same time, I also had the opportunity to make my dream a reality right here in Serbia by working on Godforged. So I chose Godforged and am still pursuing my passion, striving to make the impossible into a reality.

What are some highlights from your career?
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45091242/7339c42596c017605988f62a2c0acbe392128ae9.png
While there are numerous moments in my career that I could highlight, none compare to the first time we tried to make an RPG. At that time, we were living at a friend's house, trying to create a game from a "garage" in a sense. Although this was basically the start of our journey in the game development industry, to me, it was one of the greatest moments. Just being there, sitting in one room with friends, trying to make our first game with close to no knowledge of actually making a complete game, was incredibly memorable and impactful. The camaraderie, the shared passion, and the sheer excitement of tackling such a daunting task together made it a truly special experience.

And a big thanks to you!
If you've reached this far, we would like to extend a thank you from everyone at Tricoman Studios! Consider joining our Discord and supporting us in our journey to be a part of our story!
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45091242/8755d4ac5603fc280e38bbe087bd6f046b421f81.png

notes.title: Meet the Tricoman Team #1 - Borislav Vesnic (CEO)
notes.content:
Meet the Tricoman Team #1 - Borislav Vesnic (CEO)

From Humble Hip Hop Beginnings

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45091242/2b91028ab6196f38dc25760e70ee3861f3b37390.jpg

My journey began in the vibrant world of hip hop, where I immersed myself in composing, beat making, writing, producing, and organizing events. From collaborating with graffiti artists to managing the logistics of performances, I found my voice and honed my ability to deliver what the crowd wanted. Spending countless hours in the studio and on set, I developed a love for the creative process and the thrill of live events. These experiences not only shaped my public speaking skills but also instilled in me a passion for understanding and meeting the needs of an audience.

To Becoming a Herald of Spring

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45091242/f9593175be5fb69a48313afbcaa3804cfc5413f1.jpg

True to my name, Borislav—meaning "Fighting for Glory"—I forged my own path in the gaming industry. Determined not to succumb to the 9-5 grind, I ventured into this creative field with a vision to lead and innovate. My surname, Vesnic, is derived from Vesna, the Slavic goddess heralding spring, symbolizing my resolve to break through Serbia's harsh economic winter. I was driven to create compelling stories and designs, working with talented individuals to bring about better opportunities and a brighter future.

Foremost a Host

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45091242/d4fa1b3475a6922e0c15b28b13be976d7a61876e.jpg

As I delved deeper into the gaming industry, I made it a point to create genuine connections. Whether at events or casual meetups, I always aimed to foster meaningful relationships. My riverside cottage house became a hub for grilling, outdoor cooking, and memorable gatherings. Hosting these events allowed me to share my passion for hospitality, making friends and business partners feel welcomed and relaxed. A few shots of homemade Serbian rakia often helped even the toughest guests open up, creating a foundation of trust and camaraderie.

10 Years into the Industry

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45091242/6d4f516486a9548df322ebdb0efd494650ea9858.png

A decade into my career, I met three incredibly talented and ambitious friends who shared my passion for storytelling and RPG games. Contrary to the belief that you don't make many new friends after 35, we quickly bonded over our common goals. Recognizing a gap in the market for a standout RPG from the Balkans, we decided to join forces. We kept the name "Tricoman," which the guys originally coined, meaning "three game junkies." As the fourth member, I embraced this identity, and together, we set out to create something extraordinary.
